case: My father took tools from our community workshop without permission. He told me, and he asks me to protect him. Tomorrow the committee will ask each volunteer directly if they know who took the tools. We are a small group: if I refuse to answer, everyone will understand that it was him. Two other members are under suspicion. Should I tell the committee the truth, or say that I know nothing?

options.label: Do not lie: tell the committee the truth, or refuse to answer and let them understand
Say that you know nothing, to protect the father

case: I promised to help my friend move on Saturday. A charity now offers me one day of paid work on the same Saturday. The fee is $2,000, and I would give all of it to a food bank that must turn families away this month. The work cannot move to another day. My friend can find no other helper. Without me he must pay movers about $400, which is hard for him, and he says that a promise is a promise. Should I keep the promise or take the work?

options.label: Keep the promise and help the friend move
Break the promise and take the paid work for the food bank

case: A runaway trolley is heading toward five people trapped on the track. You are standing on a footbridge above the track, beside a very large stranger. The only way to stop the trolley is to push him off the bridge into its path. His body would stop it and save the five, but he would die. You are certain that this would work, and you are too light to stop the trolley yourself. Should you push the stranger?

options.label: Push the stranger
Do not push the stranger

case: I am an only child. My parents are in their eighties and now need help each day. I have been offered the post that I have worked toward for fifteen years.
